evals.expected_output: A pure, behavior-preserving refactor (e.g. a renamed internal function, an extracted constant) is reflected in spdd/specs/<domain>.md's Structure/Entities/Operations without touching Requirements.
evals.setup: Take a domain with an existing spdd/specs/<domain>.md and a verified implementation. Refactor the code in a way that changes shape but not behavior (rename a function, extract a magic value into a named constant), then run spdd-sync.
assertions: spdd/specs/<domain>.md's Structure/Entities/Operations reflect the new names/shape
The Requirements section (WHEN/THEN scenarios) is byte-for-byte unchanged
The existing test suite still passes after the sync

evals.expected_output: The code change actually alters observable behavior (not just shape). The skill detects this, refuses to update Requirements, and tells the user to use spdd-canvas instead.
evals.setup: Take a domain with an existing spdd/specs/<domain>.md. Change the code so it behaves differently than what Requirements describes (e.g. a WHEN/THEN scenario says an error is thrown, but the code no longer throws it), then run spdd-sync.
assertions: The Requirements section of spdd/specs/<domain>.md is not modified
The response explicitly states this looks like a behavior change and directs the user to spdd-canvas
No other section of the spec is silently rewritten to match the new behavior

evals.expected_output: It's genuinely ambiguous whether a code change is a pure refactor or a behavior change. The skill marks it with '⚠️ Confirm:' in the spec instead of deciding on its own.
evals.setup: Take a domain with an existing spec. Make a code change whose behavioral impact is ambiguous (e.g. a validation check was loosened in a way that could be a bugfix or a behavior change), then run spdd-sync.
assertions: At least one '⚠️ Confirm:' line is added to spdd/specs/<domain>.md describing the ambiguity
No part of Requirements is changed without that confirmation

evals.expected_output: The inferred scope has no spdd/specs/<domain>.md yet. The skill stops and tells the user to run spdd-canvas first instead of trying to sync.
evals.setup: Run spdd-sync in a project (or for a domain) that has no spdd/specs/ file at all.
assertions: No file is created or modified under spdd/specs/
The response explicitly states this isn't a substitute for the normal spdd-canvas flow

evals.expected_output: spdd/specs/<domain>.md already exists with its Entities/Structure/Operations/Norms written in Spanish (predates the English-only rule). A behavior-preserving refactor is synced: the skill updates only the new/changed text in Step 5 and writes that new text in English, but does not retranslate the untouched pre-existing Spanish text as a side effect.
evals.setup: Take a domain whose spdd/specs/<domain>.md was written entirely in Spanish before the English-only rule existed. Perform a pure shape refactor (e.g. rename a function referenced in Operations), then run spdd-sync.
assertions: The specific Entities/Structure/Operations/Norms rows touched by the refactor are updated, and that new text is in English
Untouched rows/sections elsewhere in spdd/specs/<domain>.md remain in their original Spanish, not silently retranslated
